SPEC-01-L3,"Purpose

FluxUI is a **full HUD overhaul**: one coherent console for combat and out-of-combat play across Classic Era, TBC Anniversary, Classic (MoP-era), and Retail Midnight. SPEC-01-L7,"What the player sees
At a glance the screen reads as one Flux console rather than many independent addons:
- **Bottom strip** — Non-combat utility grid, main action bar (with optional SHIFT/CTRL minirows), combat consumable grid, and trinket menu, sealed by a unified border.
- **Flux Window** — Fixed bottom-right docked hub with tabs for Map, Meter, Respec, and Extra Buttons.
- **Side / corner chrome** — Micro menu, status bars (gold / XP / rep), square minimap with objectives and buffs nearby, unit frames, optional raid frames.
- **Shared accent** — Class color, atlas-natural, or custom tint applied across Flux borders and related surfaces.

SPEC-01-L42,"Behaviors (product-level)
- Hides or replaces the default action bars, micro menu, and (when enabled) unit/raid frames so Flux owns those surfaces.
- Treats the bottom strip and Flux Window as one layout problem: when the window is open and UI scale is low, the strip **horizontally squeezes** so nothing collides.

SPEC-03-L31,Product rules for the rewrite

column1: 1. **Display is first-class** — Unit frames, raid frames, cast bars, and status text may continue to *look* like Flux, using paths the game allows for showing secret-aware values.

2. **No automated combat decisions** — Flux does not become a combat assistant that reads secret health/power/auras to decide actions. Assisted Combat, if present, is Blizzard’s feature surfaced as a bind—not Flux logic.

3. **Author ahead of time** — Binding conditions, restock lists, junk rules, and respec profiles are configured outside the secret decision problem; they must not depend on reading forbidden combat state to recompile mid-fight.
4. **Meters and threat** — Prefer embedding Details! or Blizzard’s native Midnight meter. Flux’s job is layout, skinning, and tab hosting—not inventing a CLEU-based meter.

5. **Nameplates** — Classic-style threat rank / level overlays that require branching on combat data stay **Classic / pre-Midnight**. On Midnight, do not promise custom threat decision overlays; stick to safe display or leave Blizzard plates alone.

6. **Settings safety** — Some Retail options/CVar writes that historically tainted nameplate or raid preview UIs should be treated as carefully deferred or skipped; players still get Flux defaults where safe.

7. **Classic unchanged in spirit** — Era, Anniversary, and Classic clients keep fuller logic where those clients still allow it. SPEC-05-L7,"What the player sees
- A **FluxUI** category in Blizzard’s Key Bindings UI for Flux-specific actions (mount, hearth, consumables, combat pots, utility slots, trinkets, reload UI, class helpers, etc.).

- The stock **Action Bar** keybind list shows **Action Buttons 1–19** as one strip (the extra seven columns keep their existing extra-bar key names under the hood). Extra-bar keybind buckets (Action Bar 2–8 / 2–5) and page-up/page-down rows are hidden on Era, Anniversary, and Classic. On Midnight the 13–19 rows are still named Action Button 13–19; leftover extra-bar *sections* may still appear in Key Bindings because Retail Settings must not be rewritten.

- Gameplay → Action Bars no longer offers “show extra bar” checkboxes on Classic-family clients. Extra bars stay off in-world on every client so Flux’s one 19-column strip is the bar the player binds.
- Optional apply/reset flows for “Flux defaults” vs leaving Blizzard settings alone.

- At very low UI scale with the Flux Window docked right, the bottom strip and related pieces **narrow (squeeze)** instead of overlapping the window.",new docs/docs/specs/05-defaults-and-bindings.md:7,7436820453d2248c84c99fff71507553efc47c19,owner-defined; see evidence,FluxDefaultSettings.lua,AUDIT-20261029,requirement recorded; compare current owner and discrepancies in FEATURE_INVENTORY.md,requirements capture; not a behavior test,pending native verification,pending matched native capture,docs/05-defaults-and-bindings.md; docs/FEATURE_INVENTORY.md; supplied source SHA256=7e2a7bb117516b3b642d6d838c15c2af00f4d680cf8010258fead6a87a424332
SPEC-05-L17,"Keybind pack (concept)
Named binds the player can assign (labels may adapt by class, e.g. conjure helpers):
- Reload UI
- Smart mount / hearth / vendor mount
- Food / water / consumables
- Combat heal pot / bandage / healthstone / mana pot / mana gem
- Assisted Combat (where the client has it)
- Class teleport; mage teleport/portal toggle and conjures
- Utility slots 1–4
- Trinket top / bottom
Most of these are **named hooks** into live Flux buttons (grids, utilities, trinkets)—the Key Bindings UI is how players assign keys; the Extra Button and Action Bar systems perform the clicks.

A default keyboard template can also seed the main action columns and multi-bar style commands so the 19-column bar is usable out of the box.",new docs/docs/specs/05-defaults-and-bindings.md:17,7436820453d2248c84c99fff71507553efc47c19,owner-defined; see evidence,FluxDefaultSettings.lua,AUDIT-20261029,requirement recorded; compare current owner and discrepancies in FEATURE_INVENTORY.md,requirements capture; not a behavior test,pending native verification,pending matched native capture,docs/05-defaults-and-bindings.md; docs/FEATURE_INVENTORY.md; supplied source SHA256=7e2a7bb117516b3b642d6d838c15c2af00f4d680cf8010258fead6a87a424332

SPEC-11-L7,"What the player sees
- A single **19-column** bottom bar: **12 main page slots + 7 “page 2” slots** on the same row (not Blizzard’s multi-bar strip layout).
- Each column can expose a **main button** plus **SHIFT and CTRL minirows** (secondary / tertiary), above or below the main row.
- **Smart promotion**: empty main faces can show content promoted from minirows so the bar stays compact until hover/drag expands layers.
- Class-colored / accent Flux border chrome on the strip.
- Up to **three corner badges per action slot** previewing alternate actions the main face is not currently showing.
- Separate **pet bar** (5×2) and **hybrid stance bar** (true forms + spell extras), placed near the player frame or stacked with status/window when the player frame is off.
- Vehicle exit control near the player frame; Retail Extra Ability HUD re-anchored near the Flux Window rather than fighting the bottom chrome.
- Blizzard default action bars are hidden/suppressed while Flux owns the strip.

- Blizzard’s own Key Bindings UI treats the strip as **Action Buttons 1–19** under the primary Action Bar header. Extra-bar show/hide options are suppressed on Classic-family clients because Flux owns one 19-column bar, not Blizzard’s multi-bar layout. Midnight still names buttons 13–19 correctly; extra-bar *sections* in Key Bindings may remain so Retail Settings preview stays untainted.

- **The Flux strip stays on screen in a vehicle.** Vehicle, possess, and override abilities page onto those same 12 columns. Blizzard’s vehicle/override bar stays Blizzard-owned (not hidden by Flux) so vehicle chrome keeps working; Flux must not Hide or EnableMouse it, or taint rides into its `SetAttribute` path.",new docs/docs/specs/11-action-bars.md:7,7436820453d2248c84c99fff71507553efc47c19,owner-defined; see evidence,Bars/Init.lua; Bars/State.lua; Bars/Layout.lua,AUDIT-20261029,requirement recorded; compare current owner and discrepancies in FEATURE_INVENTORY.md,requirements capture; not a behavior test,pending native verification,pending matched native capture,docs/11-action-bars.md; docs/FEATURE_INVENTORY.md; supplied source SHA256=c181fd52a7a6e55cde028b9d16f20e4f19662bc2ac2c31a9e3103256731770a6

SPEC-23-L9,"Profiles
Named per-character profiles that **Save** a snapshot of checked parts:
- Gear (enchant/gem/rune-aware identity)
- Talents — Classic tree learn / dual-spec swap; Retail talent loadouts on Midnight
- SoD runes (where applicable)
- Action bars (Classic; stance-bar order only on Retail loadout clients)
- Consumables preset name (links to NC consumable presets)
- Utility / binding snapshots
- Info Frame pins (character-panel pinned stats plus FPS / durability / ping)

**Save and Load are masked.** Each section and each gear/rune slot has a checkbox. Unchecked parts are not written on Save (last saved data stays) and are not applied on Load (your current setup stays). Example: only Finger 1/2 + Trinket 1/2 checked → Save updates jewelry only, Load swaps jewelry only.

Toggling a checkbox is stored immediately; you do not need to press Save just to change the mask. With **No profile** selected, the same checks stay enabled and become the mask for the next Save (new profile).
Load equips from bags (and bank when the bank is open). Two rings or trinkets with the same name each need their own copy — Flux matches by item id / enchant, not the display name.

On Retail and Forever, a profile’s gear also maps to a **Blizzard equipment set** of the same name (16-character cap). The profile dropdown and spec icon use that set’s icon.",new docs/docs/specs/23-respec.md:9,7436820453d2248c84c99fff71507553efc47c19,owner-defined; see evidence,Respec/FluxRespec_Apply.lua; Respec/FluxRespec_Core.lua,AUDIT-20261029,requirement recorded; compare current owner and discrepancies in FEATURE_INVENTORY.md,requirements capture; not a behavior test,pending native verification,pending matched native capture,docs/23-respec.md; docs/FEATURE_INVENTORY.md; supplied source SHA256=45d9728e374b9bff7ecfaf65773372231ab04fa02df27c78b696b6468168e605

SPEC-23-L58,"Blizzard equipment sets (Retail / Forever)
`C_EquipmentSet` — max **10** sets, names **16** letters. Era / Anniversary stay Flux pickup-equip.

- **Same name:** Flux profile/preset name is the Blizzard set name (truncated to 16). Character-pane sets are **imported into the Gear dropdown** on login (name, icon, items) even if Flux never saved them; Save updates that set.
- **Cap full:** a *new* name cannot create a set. Flux keeps its snapshot and equips from bags. Updating an adopted/existing set does not need a free slot.

- **Icon:** profile spec picker (and preset first-equipped-item icon) is pushed into the Blizzard set; the Gear/profile dropdowns show the live set icon and name. Renaming in the character pane renames the Flux profile/preset to match.
- **Delete:** Flux deletes the Blizzard set only if Flux created it. Adopted pre-existing sets are unlinked, not deleted.
- A profile and a preset that share a name share one Blizzard set (last Save wins).

- Extra Button equipment-set actions (`/equipset`) are unchanged.",new docs/docs/specs/23-respec.md:58,7436820453d2248c84c99fff71507553efc47c19,owner-defined; see evidence,Respec/FluxRespec_Apply.lua; Respec/FluxRespec_Core.lua,AUDIT-20261029,requirement recorded; compare current owner and discrepancies in FEATURE_INVENTORY.md,requirements capture; not a behavior test,pending native verification,pending matched native capture,docs/23-respec.md; docs/FEATURE_INVENTORY.md; supplied source SHA256=45d9728e374b9bff7ecfaf65773372231ab04fa02df27c78b696b6468168e605

SPEC-99-L1,"Glossary
Shared terms used across the FluxUI concept docs.

column3: Global color identity for Flux borders/backdrops: class, atlas-natural, or custom RGB.
NonCombat grid + main action bar + Combat grid + Trinket Menu treated as one sealed HUD.
Tint for collectibles the character has already learned, shown at vendors and similar UIs.
Blizzard helper feature surfaced as a Flux bind where the client provides it—not autonomous Flux combat logic.
Small corner preview on an action slot showing an alternate action (often from binding reverse/preview).
Docked bottom-right tabbed hub (Map, Meter, Respec, Buttons).
Clicked-style saved description of what a key/action does under conditions.
Key plus modifiers (SHIFT/CTRL/ALT combinations) routed to main, minirow, or free overrides.
Compact combat consumables row (pots, bandage, healthstone, mana, ammo, optional SBA).
Memory of best food/water/bandage/potion tiers for buttons and restock inferior marks.
Recommended CVar/keybind sets Flux can apply on setup or reset.
Named gear-only set inside Respec (smaller than a full profile).
Player-built category palettes of custom utility buttons.
Popup grid of items/mounts/spells opened from a button or macro.
Whether critical Flux default settings still match recommendations.
Narrowing the bottom strip (and related frames) so the Flux Window does not overlap at low UI scale.
Small FPS/ping/durability/stats widget with placement options.
Items marked for selling/destroying via Scrap-style rules or manual lists.
Account/character scope specifically for HUD placement preview, independent of some feature scopes.
Full Respec orchestration (talents/loadouts, gear, runes, bars, consumables, utility, bindings).
World-map-like icons mirrored onto the battlezone map.
Flux Window host for Details! or Blizzard damage meter layouts.
Flux replacement for Blizzard’s micro bar, plus Bags/Macros/Addon/Config/Reload/professions.
SHIFT or CTRL secondary/tertiary row above/below a main action column.
Out-of-combat utilities: mount, hearth, teleport, food/water, consumables, utility slots.
Swapping what the main 12 columns show for forms, stealth, vehicle, skyriding, etc.
Showing minirow content on an empty main face until layers expand.
Blocks selling/junk/DE on items required by saved Respec profiles/presets.
Desired bag count for an item or consumable tier, optionally counting bank.
SoD-oriented preset bundling runes with bars/utility.
Modifier-held overlay actions: prospect, mill, DE, open, etc.
Midnight mechanism limiting addon decision-making on combat-sensitive data while still allowing display.
Retail bonus action page while dragonriding/skyriding.

Continuous Flux chrome around the bottom console (and optional micro+status).
Four player-assignable NonCombat slots with keybinds.
Retail account-wide bank topology the inventory foundation must understand on Midnight.
